1.

The present Criminal Revision under Section 397 of the Cr.P.C. Kishore Kumar Deshmukh
has been filed by the applicant assailing order dated 23.03.2021 passed by the First Additional
Sessions Judge, Katghora in Cr.A. No. 81/2018 by which learned Appellate Court set aside the order
of acquittal dated 23.02.2018 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Katghora from
the charges under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 of the I.P.C. and remanded back the matter to the
Judicial
Magistrate
First Class

for fresh consideration after giving opportunity to the complainant.
2. The brief facts as reflected from the records are that the complainant Balram Rathore was having agricultural land in P.H.N. 54 bearing Khasra No. 927/3 Account No. 302, Area 0.26 Acres which was acquired by the SECL for Gevra Project.
He received compensation for the said land.

However,
with collusion with the revenue department and the SECL Officer the applicant, impersonating himself to be the Balram Rathore obtained job as per the rehabilitation policy of the SECL as land Kishor Kumar Dewangan vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199020988/
1 displaced persons.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On the basis of the complaint after usual investigation the case was registered as Crime No. 444/2000 for the offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 of the IPC.
The charge sheet was submitted before the Judicial Magistrate First Class which granted opportunity to lead evidence in support of their case.

The prosecution examined Vishnu Prashad Kurmi, N.L.
Bhaskar, D. Toppo and D.P. Thakur and on the basis of the statement of these witnesses and materials placed on record, learned Judicial Magistrate acquitted the accused from the charges levelled against him.
3. Being aggrieved with the said order, the complainant Balram Rathore filed Criminal Appeal under Section 372 of the Cr.P.C. Learned Appellate Court set aside the order of acquittal vide its order dated 23.02.2018 after recording its finding that learned trial Court should have given opportunity to the complainant to examine himself and to prove original records as well the complainant be also given opportunity to lead secondary evidence.
Being aggrieved with this order, the applicant has filed present criminal revision.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that learned Appellate Court has transgressed its jurisdiction and committed illegality in allowing the appeal.

Learned First Appellate Court cannot remand back the matter under Section 386(A) of the Cr.P.C. to fill up the lacunae in a routine manner unless shown such a peculiar circumstances to remand the matter.
It is for the prosecution to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt which the prosecution has miserably failed and would pray for allowing the present revision.

5. Per contra, learned counsel for the non-applicant would submit that learned First Appellate Court has not transgressed its jurisdiction and rightly recorded its finding that the complainant is the star witness.

Therefore, he should be called for evidence and the prosecution should be given opportunity for submitting original documents or in case original document is not available then secondary evidence to prove the case by the prosecution by allowing them to examine the complainant and if primary evidence is not available then they may be allowed to lead secondary evidence as the provisions are already en-grafted in the Evidence Act for allowing secondary evidence.

Learned counsel for the non-applicant would further submit that under the power conferred under Section 386(B) of the Cr.P.C. learned First Appellate Court has remanded the matter to the learned trial Court and would pray for dismissal of the present Criminal Revision.

6. After hearing the parties, this Court has granted interim protection in favour of the applicant and stayed the impugned order vide its order dated 01.07.2021.
7.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

8. Learned First Appellate Court has recorded its finding while remanding the matter to the learned trial Court that complainant be called for evidence and the prosecution be given opportunity for submitting original documents, and if original documents are not available, then the prosecution and the complainant be given opportunity to submit secondary evidence.
The learned Appellate Court has rightly reached to the conclusion that unless and until the complainant was examined, the case of the prosecution cannot be proved.

Considering this aspect of the matter, learned First Kishor Kumar Dewangan vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199020988/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Appellate Court has remanded the matter which cannot said to be suffers from illegality or irregularity in the remanding the matter.
Even otherwise, the power to interfere by this Court in the revision is very limited unless any palpable perversity or illegality is pointed out in the impugned order or in the proceeding.
The applicant has not been able to point out any such glaring illegality or irregularity committed by the learned first Appellate Court which warrants interference by this Court.
9. Accordingly, the Criminal Revision sans merits and is hereby dismissed.
The learned trial Court is directed to proceed as per the directions given by the learned Appellate Court.
